counterevidence.statement: After one successful WP206-G3 legacy recovery, mutating only the persisted recovery_provenance_ref inside f2_wp206_legacy_authority_recoveries while leaving the rebound checkpoint receipt intact is accepted by the idempotent repeat path. The repeat returns ALREADY_RECOVERED, returns the mutated provenance field, and returns the unchanged recovery_id that was originally derived over the pre-mutation provenance.
counterevidence.inference_boundary: This proves a persisted recovery-audit self-binding inconsistency at repository-hosted CI scope. It does not prove target-runtime exploitability, physical-host behavior, real-effect compromise, whole-system failure, or that the canonical owner must choose a particular repair.

relation_to_existing_counterevidence.pr689: PR689 tests conflicting caller-supplied repeat provenance while the persisted recovery row remains unchanged.
relation_to_existing_counterevidence.pr692: PR692 mutates a field already persisted in the recovery audit row after successful recovery and then tests whether the row is re-authenticated against its own recovery_id on repeat.

interpretation.stronger_question: Is f2_wp206_legacy_authority_recoveries intended to be self-authenticating append-only audit evidence on repeat, or trusted mutable metadata whose recovery_id is not revalidated after first write?
interpretation.option_a: If self-authenticating audit evidence is intended, validate the full persisted recovery record on the existing-row path, recompute/verify recovery_id over all bound fields, verify recorded DB path/device/inode, and reject conflicting provenance/tampered fields with canonical regressions.
interpretation.option_b: If the table is intentionally trusted mutable metadata after first recovery, state that explicitly, stop relying on recovery_id as an integrity claim for returned fields, and add a characterization regression so later workers do not infer append-only tamper detection.
interpretation.required_disposition: Do not open a competing WP206 mutation generation from this packet. The canonical WP206 owner/reconciliation path should disposition PR689 and PR692 together and preserve the separate same-inode live-drift threat model.

next_exact_action: Canonical WP206 ownership should explicitly disposition recovery-audit self-binding semantics using PR689 plus PR692; do not duplicate mutation authority.
